gaps.addiction: Lists were good here: two official lists (the county's Medicaid contractor, 2025, and the state's Medical Home Portal, 2023) give address and phone for about 45 providers (all recorded). Thin spots: 211's own list is only AA, NA and Al-Anon phone numbers and says to call 211; the 2019 KSL list is stale; the county's treatment-provider page loads its list by script, so it could not be read. Phones and addresses drifted between lists (First Step House, Project Reality, Altium, BAART, the CTC clinic, Huntsman), so the provider's own page mattered; about half the entries rest on a list entry alone. AA, NA and Al-Anon have no address or website recorded because no page could be read. South-valley providers (Sandy, Riverton, South Jordan) are recorded as unclear on reach.
gaps.children-pregnancy: Salt Lake County has a good official list here: the state's Maternal Resource Guide names the county's home-visiting, crisis-nursery, WIC and clinic providers with phone and address. The 211 lists give phones only and the 2021 general list is stale. Thin spots: 211 Utah's own search could not be read, so no pregnancy providers beyond these lists were found; two pregnancy-centre pages (Pregnancy Choice Utah, Planned Parenthood) would not load; and the county's only crisis pregnancy centre with a readable page is Charis. Many entries (Boys and Girls Clubs, Utah Youth Village, midwives) are unclear because their own pages returned nothing or did not state a cost. Child care, school and youth programmes beyond these were not enumerated.
gaps.clothing-household: Thin. The only 211 list with a clothing and household section is the 2021 general list (five names), and the 2024 single-parent list adds four more; both give phones only. 211 Utah's database cannot be searched from outside a browser, and no county or city list of clothing closets was found, so a missionary has few direct names beyond Deseret Industries, Catholic Community Services, Crossroads, the Salt Lake City Mission, the Rescue Mission and the Salvation Army. Furniture and bed help is almost absent: only the ReStore (low-cost), the Salvation Army (vouchers) and Sleep in Heavenly Peace (children, unverified). The address of the Salvation Army and the Mission came from their own pages, not from any list. Much Salt Lake County clothing help (Granite and Salt Lake City School District pop-up shops, Uplift Community Alliance programmes) runs through schools and referring agencies, so it is not a door a missionary can send a person to. Scout's own search would still have to do most of the work here.
gaps.disability: The Utah Parent Center's 2025 Disability Resource Book and its adult-provider list are good statewide sources with addresses and phones, but they are a nonprofit's lists, not official ones, and the 211 lists are thin (12 names, phone only, 2021). The county's own disability page lists no providers. Most Salt Lake day-training and supported-employment agencies are contracted through the state disability division (DSPD), which has a long waiting list, and their pages do not say whether a person can apply directly, so most of those are unclear. Many of the agencies' websites would not load or gave no address. Gaps: no direct list of low-cost wheelchair or medical-equipment help beyond UCAT, no readable Social Security or Deaf and Hard of Hearing division page, and no list for adult disability benefits help. Scout would still have to check each provider's own page.
gaps.domestic-violence: Lists were good for Salt Lake County: the county District Attorney's own victim-support page and the Domestic Violence Coalition name every shelter, advocate and hotline, and the state maternal guide adds counselling programmes. Where they were thin: 211 gives names and phones only (and the 2021 list is stale); no list gives the confidential shelter addresses, correctly, so people must go through a hotline; and counselling entries are mostly general mental health or offender treatment, so few of them pass. Suburb police advocates serve only their own city. Sego Lily and some city advocate pages were not read. Scout would still need to check any shelter beyond YWCA and South Valley Services, and teen dating violence and elder abuse resources were not covered.
gaps.education: Adult education is well covered by one official source, the state's Adult Education Program Directory, which gives address, phone, hours and fees for every Salt Lake County site, so ESL, GED and adult-diploma classes are the strong part. The 211 lists have no education section at all, and the only Church list found is from 2015. Thin: no list of free tutoring, children's homework help, scholarships or college-access programmes for low-income adults; no list of vocational training outside DWS and SLCC (SLCC's own pages gave only the main campus); and K-12 enrolment and homeless-student (McKinney-Vento) help were not found on any list. Several providers' own sites would not load, so those entries rest on the state directory alone. Scout would need to search for tutoring, scholarships and training.
gaps.employment: Thin. 211's county list is stale (2021) and gives only eight names and phone numbers; the state list (MIHP) and the Church's page are current but mostly name the same few agencies (the Church's employment centres, DWS, People Helping People). The real directories (211's search, DWS location pages, the Salt Lake County Library job help pages) did not load, so only a few DWS and other pages were read, and hours are mostly empty. Nothing was found for people leaving prison or jail, for day labour, for older workers (SCSEP) or for veterans; and the Ticket to Work networks are for SSI/SSDI holders only. Scout would have to do the real searching here.
gaps.financial-assistance: Thin on the central question of who still has money this month. The three official or 211 lists name only about eight programmes and give no phones or addresses for most of them, and 211's own search would not run, so the Church's page and the agencies' own sites did the work. Many agencies that give emergency rent or utility money (Catholic Community Services, St. Vincent de Paul, church and ward funds, Holy Cross Ministries, hospitals and school funds) have no readable page, and their funds run out often, so a missionary would still have to call to check. One Salvation Army address is missing and DWS's emergency fund amounts are old.
gaps.food: Lists were good for food: 211 Utah's county list names 33 pantries with address, phone and hours, and the coalition guide (October 2025) and the school district add the rest, so about 45 distinct names came out. Weak points: the 211 list is June 2024 and at least two entries have moved or changed hours (JFS, Ebenezer); the Utah Food Bank pantry map, the best live source, returns no text and could not be read; 13 names appear only on the private Plentiful directory with no phone or hours and are left unclear; the county's own food page names no pantries at all. Most pantries are church-run with no website of their own, so they were checked on the 211 entry, not the pantry's page. Scout would still have to confirm current hours.
gaps.homeless-services: Lists were not thin: the coalition's Community Resource Guide (7 October 2025) names every shelter, day centre and outreach team with phone and hours, and the shelters' own pages (homelessutah.org, The Road Home) agree. The 211 homeless list (July 2024) is a year older and several shelter phone numbers on it have changed. The confusing point is that three phone numbers circulate for the same centres (Gail Miller: 801-328-1894, 801-456-5900 and the bed line 801-990-9999) and the resource centres serve only guests with a bed, so the real way in is the bed line. Three outreach and youth programmes were read only on the coalition guide. Nothing was missing; Scout's value here is only re-checking numbers.
gaps.housing: Thin. No list names more than about a dozen housing providers for Welfare Square, and they are the same ones repeated: the county's own list, 211's general list and the Church's list all name Utah Community Action, Housing Connect, the two housing authorities, CDC of Utah, NeighborWorks, Habitat and Utah Housing Corporation. 211's housing list has no addresses, and no printable 211 housing list exists. Rent help is the real gap: Utah Community Action's funds are described as very limited, the Salt Lake City Housing Authority's rent programme is listed as not operating, and the Church list's old amounts for DWS and Crossroads are stale. Landlord-tenant help sits under legal aid and was not counted here. Most small church and charity rent funds and rent-by-the-week housing could not be confirmed, so Scout's own search still has to find them. No source gives hours for the housing authorities.
gaps.id-recovery: Official sources are good for the government doors (vital records, the Driver License Division, Social Security, the National Archives) and the fee-waiver rules are written down. The community side is thin: there is no 211 or county list of organisations that help someone get a birth certificate or ID, and the only list is the City Library's, which is reviewed twice a year but names only vouchers from VOA, Crossroads and the library social workers. The ones that could be read on their own pages (VOA, Crossroads) do not mention ID help, the Road Home's service is limited to its clients and shows as non-operational in 211, and the state's approved list of agencies that may sign the homeless verification form could not be opened. Hours and a phone were missing for the library and for the state veterans office address. Passports, tribal IDs, name changes and non-Utah birth certificates were not covered; Scout's own search would have to find these.
gaps.immigration: Immigration is well covered: three official lists name the same 10 or so Salt Lake legal agencies. Thin spots: the Salt Lake County New Americans page (the obvious county list) returned 403 and could not be read; the 211 Utah immigration guide and immigrationadvocates.org directory are interactive and were not readable; MIHP and the courts list carry stale addresses (the IRC moved from 221 S 400 W to West Valley City); several agencies' own pages give no hours or fees. No list gives reliable fee amounts, so a missionary should say 'low cost' not a price. Scout would still have to find consulates and free help for undocumented people who may not qualify for the IRC.
gaps.legal: Legal is well covered by official lists: the Courts' clinic list, the Courts' organizations list and the state refugee manual together name about 20 Salt Lake providers and the clinics have schedules. Thin spots: criminal defence and public defenders are almost absent (Salt Lake Legal Defenders Association did not load); Modest Means has no readable page with fees or phone; the Crime Victims Legal Clinic had no readable page, so its entry is weaker; clinic schedules change month to month and should be rechecked before being printed. 211 Utah's legal guide was not readable.
gaps.medical-dental-vision: Welfare Square is well served by lists for dental (211's own dental list, June 2024, with hours and fees) and for medical (the state directory and the county health department list), so about a dozen clinics could be checked. Thin spots: 211's general list names only four clinics, its health list is from 2021 and several entries have changed or closed, and the county's and 211's addresses disagree (Maliheh, Central City, Midtown). Vision has no official list at all, only a church list and Friends for Sight and EyeCare4Kids, both of which restrict who they serve. Several school and Intermountain community clinics, the Urban Indian Center and Shriners could not be confirmed. Most sites show no hours. No list says which clinics take new uninsured adults without a wait.
gaps.mental-health: Mental health was the best-covered of the five: Salt Lake County's Medicaid contractor (Optum) guide and the Utah DHHS 211 database name dozens of agencies, and the Huntsman institute flyer gives the crisis lines. But the lists are weak in three ways. The 211 Salt Lake County general list gives phone numbers only and just 11 counselling agencies. The county's own mental health page names no provider (a Resource Guide section did not load). The Optum guide is written for hospital discharge staff, so about half its entries are referral-only. The 211 search page is JavaScript and cannot be read, so 211 entries were found one at a time through web search, and private-practice therapists (hundreds) are not captured. Free and sliding-fee options are the thinnest part: Polizzi Clinic and Red Mesa counselling could not be fully checked, and none of the lists says who takes people with no insurance except Valley, VOA Cornerstone and JFS. Scout would have to do the searching for low-cost and non-Medicaid care.
gaps.reentry-support: Thin. 211's county list has no reentry heading, the county has no published reentry directory, and the only lists are the Church's page (about nine names, half outside Salt Lake County) and a private aggregator, both partly stale. The county's one real walk-in desk (JRRP, at the jail) and the Clean Slate expungement site are the solid finds; everything run by the Department of Corrections is reached through the Department, not by applying. Missing or unreadable: Persevere's own contact details, a housing-for-people-with-records list, and any employer-friendly list for Salt Lake. Scout's own search would have to find the nonprofits that serve people leaving the Salt Lake County jail and the Draper prison.
gaps.seniors: Seniors were well covered for senior centres and for the county agency: the county's own pages give address, phone and hours for 13 centres and the agency's services, and 211's list adds a few agencies. Beyond that the lists were thin. The 211 general list has only six senior entries, phone only, and two (Danville Support Services, Easterseals-Goodwill's senior employment programme) could not be confirmed. The county's printable centres PDF returned an error, so Harman (West Valley) and Sunday Anderson Westside remain unconfirmed. No list was found for home care agencies, senior housing, senior legal help or free senior transport beyond the county's Rides for Wellness; Scout would have to search for those, and for Spanish-language and refugee senior services (the county has a refugee older adults brochure that was not read).
gaps.transportation: Transportation was thin, and no single Salt Lake County list exists for it. The best sources were UTA's own pages, the Utah Medical Home Portal list (current, but only five Salt Lake entries), the Medicaid transport page and the Church's self-reliance list, which is partly stale (it still names the Hive Pass, which the city ended). The 211 Salt Lake County general list has no transportation section at all, and the 211 search page cannot be read. Help with a car (repairs, a donated car, gas) and emergency bus tickets beyond Crossroads and the Weigand Center could not be found on any current list, and the Crossroads bus-pass detail rests on the Medical Home Portal because the centre's own site no longer mentions it. Scout would have to search for car programmes, volunteer driver programmes and faith-based ride services.
gaps.utilities-phone-internet: Thin. The two 211 lists name only six and three utility providers, with phone numbers and no addresses, and there are no local lists of phone or internet help at all (neither 211 list has an internet section; Salt Lake City's page on digital resources returned 404). The real field is small: HEAT (Utah Community Action) is the one door for gas and electric, the Salvation Army is the one door for catching up a past-due bill, Crossroads is the emergency door, and the utilities themselves offer plans. The state's own HEAT pages (jobs.utah.gov) were returning errors on 4 October 2026. Lifeline phone and internet providers (Assurance, SafeLink, Xfinity) block automated page reads, so they are unclear, not passes. Scout would have to search for Lifeline-participating carriers and low-cost internet offers with a browser.
gaps.veterans: Lists were not thin for veterans in Salt Lake: the state veterans department, the VA and Workforce Services between them name most of the field, and VA programmes dominate. They are thin on the non-VA, local side: no county or city list of veteran charities was found, the Salt Lake County Veterans Service Office could only be found on aggregator pages (slco.org/veteran-services returned 404), 211 Utah's printable lists have no veterans section, and the Volunteers of America and University of Utah entries could not be confirmed on a page of their own. Several lists carry stale details (the DWS guide's old crisis-line number and Vet Center address). Veterans' food, clothing and rent help from local charities would have to come from the other categories, or from Scout's own search. 211's online search was not tried for veterans.
